newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda warns Zaire operation may get "messy".
newsitem.headline: Rwanda warns Zaire operation may get "messy".

text.p: Rwanda's president warned on Wednesday that foreign intervention in Zaire would get "messy" like previous outside military operations in Africa unless rebels were consulted.

"To the best of my knowledge the United Nations has not consulted the people controlling eastern Zaire. But in order for this operation to work they must secure the airports of Uvira, Bukavu and Goma," President Pasteur Bizimungu told Reuters.
"If they do not negotiate this with the rebels then they will be declaring war and it will be messy," the president, a member of the Hutu majority, added in an interview in Rwanda's capital Kigali.
"I have raised these concerns with the U.N. special envoy. I have raised these concerns with the international community but it looks like the United Nations hasn't learned the lessons of the past."

U.S. military intervention in Somalia from December 1992 followed by a full U.N. multinational force turned bloody in 1993 when the U.S. military came into conflict with rag-tag militia forces of late Somali warlord Mohamed Farah Aideed.

Bizimungu said he wanted to see forces approved by the U.N. Security Council to feed refugees first and then take on armed forces such as the exiled Rwandan Hutu extremist Interahamwe militia and former Rwandan troops and their Zairean allies.

"If we do not do this then we are missing the principal point of the whole operation," Bizimungu said. Asked what might happen if his concerns were ignored, he said: "This whole thing will be a mess."
There are some 1.1 million Rwandan refugees scattered by fighting in eastern Zaire who fled Rwanda in 1994 because of fear of reprisals for the Hutu genocide of up to one million people.
The refugees are mixed with Hutu militiamen and former members of the Rwandan army which led the genocide and fought alongside Zairean troops during a rebel advance two weeks ago.
Bizimungu said he was willing to meet Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko "anywhere in the world". Zaire accuses Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army of invading the east to support Tutsi rebels.
Rwandan troops entered the eastern city of Goma shortly before it fell to the rebels more than a week ago but Rwanda has said its forces are not playing a leading role as alleged by Kinshasa.

Bizimungu said Rwanda had the support of the region in its demands for a neutral multinational force which would exclude troops from France, Belgium and Rwanda because they had interests in the region.

He said Canada had proposed a force of 10,000 men to land in the Rwandan capital as well as in Kisangani, Kindu and Kinshasa in Zaire but Rwanda's government believed only a maximum of 5,000 troops were needed.
"We are consulting on that and I have made my views known to the United Nations," said Bizimungu, who has held a series of talks in recent days with U.N. Special Envoy Raymond Chretien.
